5198c12400a7: When tracking and warehouse status do not match
9900716065c3: A domestic carrier status and a warehouse order status answer different questions. A courier “delivered” scan is not proof that warehouse inspection or storage is already complete, and the public guide does not establish a universal processing deadline.
5721fcb64a39: First, compare the courier number in four places: the seller's dispatch page, the carrier record, your forwarding form, and your parcel identity card. Common user-controlled problems include a transposed digit, a marketplace order number entered instead of the courier number, or a second parcel that was never submitted. A carrier can also replace or add a last-mile number, so retain the original number and note any linked replacement rather than deleting history.
6ba7e0ba60b8: Second, ask the seller whether the order was split. “One checkout” does not mean “one box.” If there are three physical boxes, your evidence should contain three courier numbers or a clear carrier explanation of how they are related. Conversely, if a merchant consolidated several purchases into one box, do not manufacture multiple courier numbers merely to mirror the marketplace order count.
c84da5677344: Third, prepare a concise support packet if the numbers are correct but the parcel remains unmatched. Include the forwarding order ID, courier company, full domestic tracking number, delivery date shown by the carrier, sender's package count, and a non-sensitive contents summary. Hoobuy's current contact page lists online support and a customer-support email. Send only what is needed to identify the shipment; remove home addresses, payment credentials, and unrelated order details.
79fe50616844: correct your own forwarding entry when the number is wrong; ask the seller about split dispatch when package counts differ; contact support when the carrier number, forwarding ID, and confirmed package count agree but the warehouse record still cannot be matched. The public sources checked for this article do not provide a universal waiting time, so this guide does not create one.
f639fd15fee2: QC, storage, and the next shipping decision
371e0dcfe172: Hoobuy's forwarding guide states that the team categorizes products, takes QC photos, and stores them. Treat those photos as intake evidence, not a guarantee of authenticity, hidden condition, fit, or function. Check whether the visible item, colour, size label, quantity, and obvious condition match your own purchase record. If a needed angle is absent, write a precise question before requesting any available additional service. The
0f696eb751ec: explains how to turn a concern into an answerable evidence request.
0b0f4ae1ecf3: Keep the forwarding identity trail until every item is accounted for. When one incoming box becomes multiple warehouse IDs, attach each new ID to the original courier entry. When several items remain grouped, list the expected contents and mark each one as confirmed, unclear, or missing. This makes a quantity dispute easier to describe than “my order is incomplete.”
5fc59b6498f0: International parcel submission is a later decision. Forwarding does not make packaging choice, route eligibility, actual weight, or volumetric weight disappear. Once intake and QC are complete, compare the current warehouse data and live route options. Do not reuse a historical quote or assume consolidation is always cheaper; a larger box can alter chargeable weight. Continue with the
7654c876dfbd: Confirm that forwarding—not agent purchase—is the intended workflow.
71343aa203d1: Copy the warehouse address from the current forwarding page.
f542706c9883: Ask how many boxes will be sent and collect every domestic courier number.
e822612611de: Submit each number accurately and save its forwarding order ID.
da3ec2617c1a: Keep later QC or warehouse item IDs linked to the original courier entry.
e9f5b3b9fd26: Escalate with a concise evidence packet when verified records still do not match.
f395fc819cfe: Review QC, packaging, and live route information as separate decisions.
0b298bbcf99e: The best Hoobuy forwarding workflow is not the one with the most screenshots. It is the one where every physical parcel has a traceable domestic number, every submitted number has a forwarding ID, and every warehouse item can be connected back to that chain. That structure cannot prevent every seller or carrier problem, but it gives you a clean way to identify where the handoff broke and what evidence is useful next.

33432f5f4304: / Hoobuy Order ID vs Warehouse Item ID vs Parcel ID
2389cddf1bb8: ORDER RECORD · ITEM RECORD · PARCEL RECORD
f5c0690cae32: , warehouse item ID and parcel ID can all refer to the same goods at different stages, but they are not interchangeable. The order ID organizes purchasing and seller communication. A warehouse item ID represents something recorded after receipt. A parcel ID groups selected warehouse items for packing and international shipment. Carrier numbers then report physical movement outside those account records.
e6b6f96c81e4: Mixing these identifiers is one of the easiest ways to create a weak support request. This guide builds an identity chain from product selection through warehouse intake and parcel dispatch so every status, photo, message and tracking event can be tied to the correct object.
129576c4555c: Treat the order ID as the purchasing anchor
4cb181268c16: Record the order ID when the purchase instruction is created or confirmed. Attach the source listing, selected option, quantity, seller and any order note. Seller questions, price changes, purchase failures, cancellations and domestic dispatch information should remain linked to this anchor.
729255da9fde: An order ID proves that an account record exists; it does not prove a seller shipped a package. When a domestic number appears, add it as a child record. If the seller splits the order, connect every number to the same order while giving each physical package a separate row.
f182c58a27f9: Treat the warehouse item ID as the receipt anchor
64ad16410fc7: After receiving and registration, the system may create item-level records. Connect each warehouse item ID to the original order, exact variant, expected quantity and domestic package. Verify the visible title and option because similar products from different orders can be difficult to distinguish later.
fba06bed9e3f: The item record is the right place to attach warehouse status, visible inspection evidence, quantity observations and after-sale decisions. It does not replace the seller or carrier history. Keeping both layers makes it possible to show that a delivered package produced the wrong item record or that one expected item never appeared.
ae86fb1559f5: Treat the parcel ID as the packing anchor
900b2ebe7664: When stored items are selected for international shipping, the parcel ID becomes the container for that submission. Link every included warehouse item ID, packaging instruction, selected route and displayed parcel status. Preserve which items were excluded or left in storage; otherwise a missing item can be mistaken for a packing error.
22f05a37d9eb: An international tracking number should be linked under the parcel ID when it appears. The parcel ID opens the account record, while the carrier number opens movement evidence. Include both when asking about dispatch, acceptance, a route handoff or delivery.
70419d1c3a60: Map the identity chain before investigating a mismatch
8dc26205a5c5: Warehouse item ID or IDs created from receipt.
4ec2d1d5fadb: International number and any documented destination-carrier number.
a535a017e331: A complete chain can branch. One order may have several domestic packages. One package may contain several items. Several warehouse items may enter one international parcel. Your record should permit those links instead of forcing a single linear number onto the workflow.
65bd73c74a9d: Use parent and child fields in the ledger
b4106b83fd7d: For every row, label the object type and its parent. A domestic package’s parent may be an order. A warehouse item’s parents can include both the order and domestic package. A parcel’s children are the included warehouse items. This small data-model decision prevents accidental overwriting and makes filters useful.
7f0d6d888a6c: Add source system, exact label, creation time, current status and last verified event. If an identifier changes, retain the old value with a superseded note. Do not paste private addresses or payment details into the ledger. Identifiers and event evidence are usually sufficient for reconciliation.
85eb4b84be6b: One number appears on two orders
61692794df8e: Compare seller, item, variant and dispatch events. Preserve both account views and ask whether the number is legitimately shared or incorrectly assigned. Do not merge the orders yourself.
996b32418970: A warehouse item has no domestic parent
e3080c7b5de2: Search the delivered package manifest and order variants. Ask for the receipt-to-order link to be confirmed before adding the item to a parcel.
1b25cc18fdc2: A parcel manifest differs from selected items
73e2f59be4ad: Save the selection record and displayed parcel contents. Name the exact missing or extra item ID and request a packing-record check.
1d773607b330: A carrier number has no parcel link
04a7d1d5dd07: Verify the number from the parcel detail and route record. A number found in an unrelated notification is not enough to establish identity.
31177a8e7f5c: Choose the correct identifier for each support request
b9559a7ce8e4: lead with the domestic number and expected order, then list missing item IDs.
2d2351e085a4: lead with the warehouse item ID and its order/package parents.
5092a458ae79: lead with the parcel ID and included item IDs.
7aa7ea4b2fcd: lead with parcel ID plus the correct carrier number.
3c51210ae440: Include the smallest parent-child chain required to prove the mismatch. Sending every identifier in the account without labels forces the reader to reconstruct the model and increases the chance that the wrong object is investigated.
c3441c34c48b: Audit the chain at three decision points
5b19f49fdef2: After seller dispatch, verify that every domestic number is attached to the intended order. After warehouse intake, verify that every item ID maps to the expected variant and package. Before parcel submission, verify that the parcel contains the intended item IDs and no unresolved warehouse exception. After dispatch, connect the international number to the correct parcel.
4fef013e14b5: These checks are faster than rebuilding the chain after a mismatch. They also help you decide whether a problem belongs to purchasing, domestic delivery, intake, packing or a carrier handoff.
